"""Pydantic models defining the structured JSON stored in tfc_scenarios.content.

These models validate scenario data authored by the GM and serve as the
bridge between the scenario editor and the exercise engine.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from pydantic import BaseModel, Field, model_validator

from core.game_mode_constants import GM_CLASSIC, GM_SIMPLE_COLLABORATIVE


class SystemEffectDef(BaseModel):
    """A system state change triggered by selecting a decision option or event start."""

    system_id: str
    operational_state: str | None = None  # "green" | "yellow" | "red"
    power_state: bool | None = None
    set_all_power: bool = False  # General Quarters: power all systems ON


class DomainEffectDef(BaseModel):
    """A warfare domain threat-level change triggered by an event."""

    domain_id: str
    threat_level: str  # "green" | "yellow" | "red"


class DecisionOptionDef(BaseModel):
    """A single selectable option within a decision template."""

    id: str
    label: str
    score: float = 0.0
    stress_delta: int = 0
    system_effects: list[SystemEffectDef] = []
    targets_system: bool = False
    max_plays: int = Field(default=0, ge=0)  # 0 = unlimited, 1+ = explicit limit


class DecisionTemplateDef(BaseModel):
    """Template for a decision that players must make during an exercise."""

    id: str
    title: str
    description: str = ""
    issue_id: str  # linked issue
    question_type: str  # single_choice, multi_choice, free_text, scale
    options: list[DecisionOptionDef] = []
    completion_mode: str = "first_response"
    timeout_ms: float = 0  # 0 = no timeout
    target_roles: list[str] = []
    forced_option_ids: list[str] = []
    max_selections: int | None = None  # None = unlimited
    stress_delta: int = 0  # turn-level stress applied regardless of card choice


class ScenarioEventDef(BaseModel):
    """Definition of an inject (event) within a scenario. Domain term: 'inject'."""

    id: str
    title: str
    description: str = ""
    event_type: str  # informational, operational, decision
    scheduled_pt_ms: float  # when to trigger in play time
    duration_ms: float | None = None  # auto-complete after duration
    dependencies: list[str] = []  # event IDs that must complete first
    triggered_issues: list[str] = []  # issue IDs activated on completion
    target_roles: list[str] = []  # empty = visible to all roles
    role_descriptions: dict[str, str] = {}  # per-role description overrides
    system_effects: list[SystemEffectDef] = []  # system state changes on event start
    domain_effects: list[DomainEffectDef] = []  # warfare domain changes on event start


class ScenarioIssueDef(BaseModel):
    """Definition of a defect (issue) within a scenario. Domain term: 'defect'."""

    id: str
    title: str
    description: str = ""
    trigger_mode: str  # time-based, event-based, manual
    trigger_time_pt_ms: float | None = None
    trigger_event_id: str | None = None
    auto_resolve_ms: float = 0  # 0 = no auto-resolve


class ScenarioPhaseDef(BaseModel):
    """Definition of a phase grouping events within a scenario."""

    id: str
    title: str
    description: str = ""
    duration_ms: float | None = None  # auto-advance after duration
    events: list[str] = []  # event IDs in this phase


class SystemStateDef(BaseModel):
    """Initial or expected system state in scenario definition."""

    system_id: str
    label: str = ""
    category: str = "system"  # "system" | "weapon"
    operational_state: str | None = None  # "green"|"yellow"|"red"
    power_state: bool | None = None


class WarfareDomainDef(BaseModel):
    """Initial warfare domain definition in scenario."""

    domain_id: str
    label: str = ""
    initial_threat_level: str = "green"


class BlueCardDef(BaseModel):
    """A card in the global catalog, independent of any turn."""

    id: str
    title: str
    description: str = ""
    targets_system: bool = False


class TurnInjectDef(BaseModel):
    """Per-role inject text within a turn."""

    target_roles: list[str] = []
    text: str
    role_descriptions: dict[str, str] = {}


class TurnCardConfig(BaseModel):
    """Per-turn configuration for an available blue card."""

    card_id: str
    score: float = 0.0
    stress_delta: int = 0
    system_effects: list[SystemEffectDef] = []
    domain_effects: list[DomainEffectDef] = []
    max_plays: int = Field(default=0, ge=0)


class PathNoteDef(BaseModel):
    """Facilitator notes for best/acceptable play paths."""

    card_ids: list[str] = []
    notes: str = ""


class TurnDefinition(BaseModel):
    """Groups injects and a decision template into a turn."""

    turn_index: int
    title: str = ""
    facilitator_prompt: str | None = None
    has_decisions: bool = True
    duration_ms: float | None = None
    # Legacy fields (kept for backward compat with existing seeds)
    inject_ids: list[str] = []
    decision_template_id: str | None = None
    # New turn-authoring fields
    injects: list[TurnInjectDef] = []
    available_cards: list[TurnCardConfig] = []
    max_selections: int = 2
    base_stress_delta: int = 0
    system_effects_on_start: list[SystemEffectDef] = []
    domain_effects_on_start: list[DomainEffectDef] = []
    best_path: PathNoteDef | None = None
    acceptable_path: PathNoteDef | None = None
    design_notes: str = ""


class RoleDef(BaseModel):
    """Definition of a participant role within a scenario."""

    id: str
    label: str
    player_type: str = "advisor"  # "advisor" or "decision_maker"


class ScenarioContent(BaseModel):
    """Top-level scenario definition validated against this schema.

    This is the structured JSON stored in the ``tfc_scenarios.content``
    column. The GM authors this via the scenario editor; the engine
    loader converts it into runtime objects at exercise start.
    """

    phases: list[ScenarioPhaseDef] = []
    events: list[ScenarioEventDef] = []
    issues: list[ScenarioIssueDef] = []
    decision_templates: list[DecisionTemplateDef] = []
    default_time_factor: float = 1.0
    briefing: str = ""
    objectives: list[str] = []
    rules: list[str] = []
    game_mode: str = GM_CLASSIC
    game_mode_config: dict[str, object] = {}
    decision_sequence: list[str] = []
    roles: list[RoleDef] = []
    turns: list[TurnDefinition] = []
    initial_system_states: list[SystemStateDef] = []
    initial_warfare_domains: list[WarfareDomainDef] = []
    score_tier_thresholds: dict[str, float] = {}  # {"lo": 0.33, "mid": 0.66}
    stress_effect_preset: str = "standard"  # "off" | "mild" | "standard" | "intense"

    @model_validator(mode="after")
    def validate_roles(self) -> ScenarioContent:
        """Enforce that every scenario defines roles appropriate for its game mode."""
        if not self.roles:
            raise ValueError("Scenario must define at least one role in 'roles'.")
        role_ids = {r.id for r in self.roles}
        player_types = {r.player_type for r in self.roles}
        if "decision_maker" not in player_types:
            raise ValueError(
                "Scenario must have at least one role with player_type='decision_maker'."
            )
        if self.game_mode == GM_SIMPLE_COLLABORATIVE and len(self.roles) < 2:
            raise ValueError(
                "Simple collaborative scenarios require at least 2 playable "
                f"roles, but only {len(self.roles)} defined."
            )
        for dt in self.decision_templates:
            for rid in dt.target_roles:
                if rid not in role_ids:
                    raise ValueError(
                        f"Decision template '{dt.id}' targets unknown "
                        f"role '{rid}'. Defined roles: {sorted(role_ids)}."
                    )
        for evt in self.events:
            for rid in evt.target_roles:
                if rid not in role_ids:
                    raise ValueError(
                        f"Event '{evt.id}' targets unknown "
                        f"role '{rid}'. Defined roles: {sorted(role_ids)}."
                    )
            for rid in evt.role_descriptions:
                if rid not in role_ids:
                    raise ValueError(
                        f"Event '{evt.id}' has role_description for unknown "
                        f"role '{rid}'. Defined roles: {sorted(role_ids)}."
                    )
        return self

Here's my honest assessment of the schema's fitness for LLM-directed scenario generation:

## What's well designed

**Strong structural separation.** The DomainConfig / ScenarioContent split is the single best design choice. An LLM gets the vocabulary (systems, roles, blue cards, warfare domains) from the domain config and only needs to compose the narrative (events, turns, decisions) in the scenario. This dramatically reduces the generation surface area.

**Pydantic validation as guardrails.** The `model_validator` on `ScenarioContent` catches cross-reference errors (role IDs, event IDs) at parse time. An LLM that generates structurally valid JSON gets immediate feedback if it references a non-existent role — this is exactly what you want for an iterative generate-validate loop.

**Rich exemplar.** Silent Wake at ~927 lines is a complete, realistic scenario. It works as a few-shot example — an LLM can pattern-match against it directly.

**Flat-ish type hierarchy.** Most types are 1-2 levels deep. No recursive structures, no polymorphic unions. LLMs handle this well.

## What will cause problems

### 1. Dual authoring paths create ambiguity

`TurnDefinition` has both legacy fields (`inject_ids`, `decision_template_id`) and new fields (`injects`, `available_cards`). Silent Wake uses only the legacy path. An LLM won't know which to use — and the schema doesn't enforce mutual exclusivity. You'll get generation where it mixes both, or uses the legacy path because that's what the exemplar shows.

**Fix:** Either add a `model_validator` that rejects mixed usage, or migrate Silent Wake to the new path so the exemplar demonstrates the intended authoring model.

### 2. Implicit ID contracts with no enum constraints

`system_id`, `domain_id`, `card_id` are all bare strings. There's no validation that a `system_effects[].system_id` in a decision option actually exists in `initial_system_states`. Same for `domain_effects[].domain_id` vs `initial_warfare_domains`. The role validator exists, but system/domain cross-referencing is missing.

An LLM will invent system IDs that don't exist in the domain config. This is the #1 most likely generation failure mode.

**Fix:** Add `model_validator`s that check system_id and domain_id references against the initial state lists — same pattern as the role validator.

### 3. No field-level descriptions in the schema

Pydantic models have class docstrings but no `Field(description=...)` on individual fields. When you export to JSON Schema (for the planned "metadata header"), fields like `completion_mode`, `trigger_mode`, `question_type`, `stress_effect_preset` will appear as bare strings with no valid-values documentation.

An LLM has to guess that `completion_mode` is `"first_response"` or `"consensus"` — or that `operational_state` is `"green" | "yellow" | "red"`. These are the exact kind of closed enums that cause hallucination when undocumented.

**Fix:** Use `Literal` types or `Field(description=..., json_schema_extra={"enum": [...]})` for all string-enum fields. This is probably the highest-ROI change.

### 4. Event ↔ Decision ↔ Turn coupling is fragile

The current schema has events, decision_templates, and turns all keyed by ID, with turns pointing at events and decisions via `inject_ids` / `decision_template_id`. Plus `decision_sequence` is a separate ordered list. This is 4 parallel structures that must stay synchronized.

An LLM will get the cross-references wrong. It's the "foreign key without a database" problem.

**Fix:** The new `TurnDefinition` model with inline `injects` and `available_cards` is the right direction — it collapses the parallel structures. But until Silent Wake actually uses it, the exemplar teaches the wrong pattern.

### 5. Magic values

- `"__all__"` as a `system_id` in General Quarters (`set_all_power: true`) 
- `max_plays: 0` means unlimited (not zero)
- `timeout_ms: 0` means no timeout
- `auto_resolve_ms: 0` means no auto-resolve

These sentinel values are LLM traps. The model will interpret `0` literally.

**Fix:** Use `None`/`null` for "not set" and document the semantics.

## Bottom line

The schema is **good enough to work with guided prompting** (system prompt that explains the constraints + Silent Wake as example). It is **not yet self-describing enough for unguided generation** from the JSON Schema alone.

The highest-leverage changes, in order:

1. **Literal types for string enums** — prevents the most common hallucination
2. **Cross-reference validators for system_id/domain_id** — catches the second most common error
3. **Migrate Silent Wake to new turn model** — so the exemplar teaches the right pattern
4. **Enforce legacy/new mutual exclusivity** on TurnDefinition
5. **Replace 0-means-unlimited sentinels** with explicit `None`

Changes 1-2 are probably a few hours of work and would make the schema dramatically more LLM-friendly. The schema architecture itself is sound — it's the type strictness and documentation layer that needs tightening.

1→# Scenario Creation Flow — Design
     2→
     3→## Goal
     4→
     5→Design the user flow for creating a TFC scenario from scratch, optimized for Naval Group facilitators who understand Silent Wake game mechanics (turns, injects, blue cards, stress, systems).
     6→
     7→## Key Insight
     8→
     9→Facilitators create **new narratives on reusable foundations**. Roles, systems, warfare domains, and the blue card catalog are mostly stable across scenarios. What changes is the story — which injects happen when, which cards are available each turn, and what the consequences are.
    10→
    11→## Architecture Decision
    12→
    13→**DomainConfig becomes the reusable foundation.** A single DomainConfig (e.g., "Silent Wake") holds the shared catalogs. Scenarios reference it and only define the turn-by-turn narrative. This replaces the current approach where every entity is duplicated inside each scenario's `ScenarioContent` JSON.
    14→
    15→---
    16→
    17→## The Creation Flow
    18→
    19→### Phase 1 — Pick Your Foundation (5 seconds)
    20→
    21→Single screen. The DomainConfig (Silent Wake) is pre-selected since there is only one.
    22→
    23→**What the facilitator sees:**
    24→- Foundation name and description
    25→- Summary stats: "7 roles · 6 systems · 5 weapons · 4 warfare domains · 22 blue cards"
    26→- Expandable preview of each catalog (roles table, systems table, cards table, etc.)
    27→- Inline add/edit for any catalog item (changes apply to the foundation globally, affecting all future scenarios)
    28→
    29→**No "Create New Domain" flow.** Out of scope. Single foundation, editable in place.
    30→
    31→**Actions:**
    32→- "Continue" → Phase 2
    33→
    34→---
    35→
    36→### Phase 2 — Scenario Setup (5–10 minutes)
    37→
    38→Single scrollable form for scenario-level metadata.
    39→
    40→**Fields:**
    41→
    42→| Field | Type | Required | Notes |
    43→|-------|------|----------|-------|
    44→| Title | text | yes | |
    45→| Description | textarea | no | Short summary for scenario list |
    46→| Briefing | rich textarea | yes | Full context read to players before Turn 1 |
    47→| Objectives | ordered list | yes | Add/remove/reorder |
    48→| Rules | ordered list | no | Add/remove/reorder |
    49→| Game Mode | toggle | yes | Classic / Simple Collaborative |
    50→| Score Tier Thresholds | two number inputs | no | lo/mid boundaries (e.g., 0.33, 0.66) |
    51→
    52→**Initial State Overrides:**
    53→
    54→Below the metadata, the foundation's systems and warfare domains are shown with their default initial states. The author can override per-scenario:
    55→
    56→- System initial power state (ON/OFF) and operational state (Green/Yellow/Red)
    57→- Warfare domain initial threat level (Green/Red — binary, two states only)

   118→## Development Commands

   122→make dev-tfc-local        # DB + TFC API in Docker, Angular natively (instant HMR)

   132→TFC uses the same `AppError` hierarchy as the main app (see `core/exceptions.py`). Services raise domain exceptions; the middleware in `core/middleware.py` translates them into JSON responses.

   138→| `ForbiddenError` | 403 | Insufficient permissions |

1→# Scenario Creation Flow — Design
     2→
     3→## Goal
     4→
     5→Design the user flow for creating a TFC scenario from scratch, optimized for Naval Group facilitators who understand Silent Wake game mechanics (turns, injects, blue cards, stress, systems).
     6→
     7→## Key Insight
     8→
     9→Facilitators create **new narratives on reusable foundations**. Roles, systems, warfare domains, and the blue card catalog are mostly stable across scenarios. What changes is the story — which injects happen when, which cards are available each turn, and what the consequences are.
    10→
    11→## Architecture Decision
    12→
    13→**DomainConfig becomes the reusable foundation.** A single DomainConfig (e.g., "Silent Wake") holds the shared catalogs. Scenarios reference it and only define the turn-by-turn narrative. This replaces the current approach where every entity is duplicated inside each scenario's `ScenarioContent` JSON.
    14→
    15→---
    16→
    17→## The Creation Flow
    18→
    19→### Phase 1 — Pick Your Foundation (5 seconds)
    20→
    21→Single screen. The DomainConfig (Silent Wake) is pre-selected since there is only one.
    22→
    23→**What the facilitator sees:**
    24→- Foundation name and description
    25→- Summary stats: "7 roles · 6 systems · 5 weapons · 4 warfare domains · 22 blue cards"
    26→- Expandable preview of each catalog (roles table, systems table, cards table, etc.)
    27→- Inline add/edit for any catalog item (changes apply to the foundation globally, affecting all future scenarios)
    28→
    29→**No "Create New Domain" flow.** Out of scope. Single foundation, editable in place.
    30→
    31→**Actions:**
    32→- "Continue" → Phase 2
    33→
    34→---
    35→
    36→### Phase 2 — Scenario Setup (5–10 minutes)
    37→
    38→Single scrollable form for scenario-level metadata.
    39→
    40→**Fields:**
    41→
    42→| Field | Type | Required | Notes |
    43→|-------|------|----------|-------|
    44→| Title | text | yes | |
    45→| Description | textarea | no | Short summary for scenario list |
    46→| Briefing | rich textarea | yes | Full context read to players before Turn 1 |
    47→| Objectives | ordered list | yes | Add/remove/reorder |
    48→| Rules | ordered list | no | Add/remove/reorder |
    49→| Game Mode | toggle | yes | Classic / Simple Collaborative |
    50→| Score Tier Thresholds | two number inputs | no | lo/mid boundaries (e.g., 0.33, 0.66) |
    51→
    52→**Initial State Overrides:**
    53→
    54→Below the metadata, the foundation's systems and warfare domains are shown with their default initial states. The author can override per-scenario:
    55→
    56→- System initial power state (ON/OFF) and operational state (Green/Yellow/Red)
    57→- Warfare domain initial threat level (Green/Red — binary, two states only)
    58→
    59→Overrides apply to this scenario only. Foundation defaults remain unchanged.
    60→
    61→**Actions:**
    62→- "Continue to Turns" → Phase 3
    63→- "Save Draft" → saves without turns
    64→
    65→---
    66→
    67→### Phase 3 — Turn-by-Turn Authoring (the core)
    68→
    69→Where the facilitator spends 90% of their time.
    70→
    71→**Layout:** Split panel. Left: turn timeline. Right: turn editor.
    72→
    73→#### Left Panel — Turn Timeline
    74→
    75→- Vertical list of turns: Turn 0, Turn 1, Turn 2, ...
    76→- Each turn shows: index, title, colored pip for stress delta (+0 green, +1/+2 amber, -1 blue)
    77→- "Add Turn" button at the bottom
    78→- Drag to reorder (auto-renumbers `turn_index`)
    79→- Duplicate and delete actions per turn
    80→- Click a turn to edit it in the right panel
    81→
    82→#### Right Panel — Turn Editor
    83→
    84→A single turn has these sections, top to bottom:
    85→
    86→**1. Turn Header**
    87→
    88→| Field | Type | Notes |
    89→|-------|------|-------|
    90→| Turn index | read-only | Auto-numbered |
    91→| Title | text | e.g., "Steady Approach", "Unexpected Current" |
    92→| Facilitator prompt | textarea | What the facilitator reads aloud |
    93→| Has decisions | toggle | Turn 0 defaults to false. Hides blue card section when off |
    94→| Duration (ms) | number | Only shown when `has_decisions: false` (e.g., Turn 0 = 15 min) |
    95→
    96→**2. Injects**
    97→
    98→List of inject entries. Each inject:
    99→- **Target role(s)** — pick from foundation's role catalog (single role, multiple, or "all")
   100→- **Inject text** — the situation update for that role
   101→- Not every role gets an inject every turn — only add what's needed
   102→
   103→**3. Available Blue Cards** (hidden when `has_decisions: false`)
   104→
   105→The foundation's card catalog shown as a checklist. Tick cards available this turn. For each selected card, an expandable configuration row:
   106→
   107→| Field | Type | Notes |
   108→|-------|------|-------|
   109→| Score | number | Points for picking this card this turn (+/−/0) |
   110→| Stress delta | int | Stress change if picked (+1, −1, 0) |
   111→| System effects | list | system_id → new operational_state or power_state |
   112→| Domain effects | list | domain_id → new threat level |
   113→| Targets system | read-only | Inherited from catalog. If true, player picks target at play time |
   114→| Max plays | int | Times this card can be played this turn (0 = unlimited) |
   115→
   116→**Max selections per turn:** Number input, default 2 (how many cards CO can pick).
   117→
   118→**4. Turn Consequences**
   119→
   120→Effects that happen at turn start, independent of card choice:
   121→- Base stress delta (applied regardless of card choice)
   122→- System effects on turn start (e.g., "COMMS → Yellow" from the inject narrative)
   123→- Domain effects on turn start (e.g., "CYBER → red")
   124→
   125→**5. Facilitator Notes** (optional)
   126→
   127→| Field | Type | Notes |
   128→|-------|------|-------|
   129→| Best path | Card IDs + notes | Which cards are optimal, expected outcome |
   130→| Acceptable path | Card IDs + notes | Suboptimal but valid alternative |
   131→| Design notes | free text | Why this turn exists, what it teaches |
   132→
   133→#### Turn 0 — Special Case
   134→
   135→Turn 0 (Pre-Sail Briefing) is auto-created with:
   136→- `has_decisions: false`
   137→- Blue card section hidden
   138→- Duration field visible (default 15 min)
   139→- Injects are briefing cards (background context per role), not situation updates
   140→
   141→The facilitator can create non-decision turns at other indices by toggling `has_decisions: false`.
   142→
   143→---
   144→
   145→## Data Model Changes
   146→
   147→### DomainConfig — New Fields
   148→
   149→Add three new JSON fields to `tfc_domain_configs`:
   150→
   151→```python
   152→systems: list[SystemStateDef]        # Ship systems + weapons with default initial states
   153→warfare_domains: list[WarfareDomainDef]  # Warfare domains with default initial threat levels
   154→blue_card_catalog: list[BlueCardDef]     # Global card definitions
   155→```
   156→
   157→The existing `roles`, `terminology`, `theme`, `severity_levels` fields remain.
   158→
   159→### New Model: BlueCardDef
   160→
   161→A card in the global catalog, independent of any turn:
   162→
   163→```python
   164→class BlueCardDef(BaseModel):
   165→    id: str                    # e.g., "SWB01"
   166→    title: str                 # e.g., "Continue Mission"
   167→    description: str = ""      # What this card does generically
   168→    targets_system: bool = False  # Whether player picks target system at play time
   169→```
   170→
   171→### ScenarioContent Changes
   172→
   173→- `roles` — removed (inherited from DomainConfig)
   174→- `initial_system_states` — becomes optional overrides only (if absent, use DomainConfig defaults)
   175→- `initial_warfare_domains` — becomes optional overrides only (if absent, use DomainConfig defaults)
   176→- `decision_templates` and `events` — **generated** from the turn definitions at save/load time. The editor writes `turns[]` and derives the rest.
   177→- `turns` array becomes the primary authored structure
   178→
   179→### TurnDefinition — Expanded
   180→
   181→```python
   182→class TurnInjectDef(BaseModel):
   183→    target_roles: list[str] = []   # Empty = all roles
   184→    text: str                       # The inject content
   185→    role_descriptions: dict[str, str] = {}  # Per-role text overrides
   186→
   187→class TurnCardConfig(BaseModel):
   188→    card_id: str               # References BlueCardDef.id in DomainConfig
   189→    score: float = 0.0
   190→    stress_delta: int = 0
   191→    system_effects: list[SystemEffectDef] = []
   192→    domain_effects: list[DomainEffectDef] = []
   193→    max_plays: int = 0         # 0 = unlimited
   194→
   195→class PathNoteDef(BaseModel):
   196→    card_ids: list[str] = []
   197→    notes: str = ""
   198→
   199→class TurnDefinition(BaseModel):
   200→    turn_index: int

This is actually quite well thought out. Here's my assessment of the `_llm_schema` JSON export specifically:

## What works well

**The foundation vocabulary is inlined.** Lines 44-58 — the LLM gets the exact IDs, labels, and categories for roles, systems, domains, and blue cards. This is the #1 thing an LLM needs to avoid hallucinating IDs. Smart.

**The instructions are prescriptive, not descriptive.** Line 29-42 — "Card IDs must reference...", "Role IDs must reference..." — these are constraints, not just documentation. LLMs follow constraints better than they infer rules from examples.

**Enums are explicit.** Lines 87-93 — `operational_state`, `threat_level`, `game_mode`, etc. are listed as closed sets. This directly prevents the most common generation failures.

**Turn structure is documented with inline type hints.** Lines 61-85 — each field gets a type and a brief semantic description. Good enough for an LLM to generate valid structure without needing the full Pydantic schema.

## Gaps worth addressing

**1. Missing enums.** `threat_level` only lists `["green", "red"]` but the backend accepts `"yellow"` too (see [scenario_content.py:27](apps/tfc/backend/features/scenario/scenario_content.py#L27) — `DomainEffectDef` has `# "green" | "yellow" | "red"`). Silent Wake uses yellow extensively (e.g., cyber domain in turn 5). An LLM following the export schema would never produce yellow threat levels.

**2. `stress_effect_preset` missing from enums.** The top-level `content` field `stress_effect_preset` (`"off" | "mild" | "standard" | "intense"`) isn't documented anywhere in the export.

**3. No top-level content structure doc.** The `turn_structure` describes turns in detail, but there's no equivalent for the `content` object itself. Fields like `briefing`, `objectives`, `rules`, `score_tier_thresholds`, `initial_system_states`, `initial_warfare_domains`, `game_mode_config` are undocumented in the export. An LLM has to reverse-engineer them from the content blob.

**4. Card effects not documented in the catalog.** `available_cards[]` can carry `system_effects` and `domain_effects`, but the `turn_structure` description (line 72) only mentions `{card_id, score, stress_delta}`. The LLM won't know cards can trigger system/domain changes.

**5. No example turn.** The instructions explain the structure but don't include a minimal concrete example. A single 5-line example turn in the instructions string would anchor the LLM better than paragraphs of description.

**6. Legacy fields not explicitly excluded.** The instructions say "content.turns is the primary authoring structure" but don't say "do NOT populate events, issues, decision_templates, phases, or decision_sequence — those are legacy." An LLM seeing both structures in the content will likely try to populate both.

## Verdict

This is genuinely good for a v1. The foundation inlining + enum listing + constraint-based instructions hit the three highest-leverage things for LLM generation. The gaps are all fixable additions:

| Fix | Effort | Impact |
|-----|--------|--------|
| Add `"yellow"` to `threat_level` enum | 1 line | Prevents broken scenarios |
| Add `stress_effect_preset` to enums | 1 line | Prevents hallucination |
| Add `content_structure` dict (like `turn_structure`) | ~15 lines | Documents top-level fields |
| Expand `available_cards[]` description to include effects | 1 line | Prevents missing card effects |
| Add explicit "do NOT populate legacy fields" instruction | 1 sentence | Prevents dual-path confusion |
| Add one example turn in instructions | ~10 lines | Best single improvement for generation quality |

The architecture decision to embed the schema *inside the export file* rather than as a separate document is the right call — it means any exported JSON is self-contained and an LLM can work from the file alone without needing external documentation.
